fixtures: Five new paired three-file projects. Each must initially have no green single edit, at least two green cross-file pairs and a complete search in both languages. Qualify this property using only initial public data. Count every timed attempt after qualification.
search: Use the existing TIDE --pairs --probes and the unchanged external CPython comparator from experiment 61. Same 32 single-edit and 64 cross-file pair budgets. Look for the first valid disagreement over the same ordered pool, up to 32 inputs and 128 candidate evaluations per search.
resolution: Generate one pool per timed attempt. Confirm the first disagreement by calling only the public TIDE contract function for that input. Add it to the visible tests and remove it from the pool. Run the same complete filter again. Allow up to three confirmations on each side, rerunning without probes after the third. Stop at one green pair. Count no valid split, truncation, a non-singleton final shortlist, or failed acceptance as failed repair.
acceptance: Preview both edits together and materialize the two validated files in a fresh scratch project. Reopen the result and check every public test plus 72 disjoint, held-out cases. The search and confirmation steps never receive held-out expectations.
timer: Same monotonic wall-clock interval as experiment 61. From before pool generation through diagnosis, all pair searches, confirmations, test additions, scans, patch preview, source writes and final acceptance or abstention. Outside the timer are tool builds, fixture staging and initial and hidden case generation.
repetitions: One qualification pair and then 12 timed pairs per family. Alternate TIDE/Python-AST precedence within each family, rotate task order each round, fresh scratch copies and fresh CLI invocations, sequential on one logical CPU with warm filesystem caches.
accounting: Report successes over all attempts, token sum, end-to-end median and nearest-rank P95, median paired speed ratio and dispersion, initial green counts, confirmation counts and per-family outcomes. Use no model.
